comparator.name: Mathematics
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from VU Amsterdam's current official sources for 2026-2027: the Mathematics curriculum page, the programme's 2026-2027 Teaching and Examination Regulations (TER, section B2, Articles 10-12), the 2026-2027 study guide for the programme (including its course list with EC weights) and the official study-paths overview linked from that study guide. Year 1 consists of eleven compulsory credit-bearing courses totalling 60 EC (two of them, Introduction to Mathematical Modelling, LaTeX and Mathematica and Introduction to Programming (Python), are 3-EC units); the zero-credit English Language Test is a compulsory diagnostic test, not a 180-EC component. Year 2 contains five compulsory courses (Mathematical Statistics, Numerical Methods, Fourier Analysis, Mathematical Modelling of Stochastic Systems, Dynamical Systems) and a period-6 constrained choice between Elements of Geometry and Probabilistic Forecasting for Dynamical Systems. Year 3 contains at least 30 EC of semester-5 electives or a minor, preserved as open profiling space, and the compulsory Bachelor Project Mathematics (12 EC), History of Science (3 EC) and Philosophy and Ethics (3 EC). The remaining 36 EC in years 2 and 3 are constrained mathematics choices (at least two from a TER list) and interdisciplinary electives. TER Article 10.2 states that the programme has no formal specialisations; the study guide presents seven named 2026-2027 study paths as non-binding, conflict-free course selections that automatically meet the programme requirements. One path is instantiated under the neutral route rule (see routeSelection): the Algebra and Geometry path, whose conflict-free choices are Rings and Fields, Complex Analysis, Topology and Galois Theory in year 2, Elements of Geometry as the period-6 choice, and Differential Topology and Partial Differential Equations in year 3 (Functional Analysis is listed as a further option that may clash). The path also suggests Differential Geometry, Number Theory, Measure Theory, Non-linear Dynamical Systems and Project Computer Assisted Proofs for semester 5, but that semester is free elective space and is kept open. Source discrepancy: the curriculum webpage still lists Project Mathematics among year-2 courses, whereas the 2026-2027 TER records Project Mathematics as discontinued (last offered 2022-2023) and replaced by the period-6 constrained choice; the formally adopted TER is followed. Limitation: individual 2026-2027 course descriptions in the study guide could not be retrieved automatically, so comparator content is characterised from course titles, the curriculum page and the TER rather than from course outlines.

alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to VU's Mathematics bachelor: the complete UCR mathematics sequence in calculus, linear algebra, discrete mathematics and logic, probability and statistics, numerical methods and linear dynamical systems, programmed in Python and carried into algorithms, optimisation and the modelling of real natural and physical systems, with philosophy and ethics of knowledge. It reproduces the pure-and-applied, modelling-oriented core as far as UCR allows and leaves VU's proof-based analysis, abstract algebra, geometry and topology as honest gaps.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum rests on UCR's full mathematics sequence (Mathematical Methods, Linear Algebra, Advanced Calculus, Logic & Discrete Mathematics, Probability & Statistics, Computational & Numerical Methods, Linear Systems) with three further statistics courses, and adds two strands: computation and optimisation (Introduction to Programming, Algorithms & Data Structures, Advanced Algorithms, Optimization Methods in AI, Decision-making in AI) and the modelling of real systems (ecology, epidemiology, Earth-system modelling, robotics and image processing), closed by philosophy and ethics. The label names mathematics together with these two strands. It deliberately does not claim to be a full mathematics degree: UCR has no proof-based analysis, abstract algebra, geometry or topology course, which the comparator's selected Algebra and Geometry path emphasises.

alternatives.concept: A mathematics programme organised around VU's Probability and Statistics and Data Science study paths: the shared calculus, linear-algebra, probability and numerical foundation is carried into statistical inference and multivariate modelling, econometric estimation, data management and machine learning, and applied to image, satellite and population-health data, with attention to the ethics of data and algorithms.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum keeps the shared mathematics sequence and builds on it a statistics and data-science strand of eleven courses: Research Methods & Statistics, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Econometrics, Introduction to Data Science, Database Management Systems, Machine Learning, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Reinforcement Learning, Image Processing & Computer Vision, Earth Observation and AI Ethics, with epidemiology as a data-rich application. Mathematics and the statistics/data strand are of comparable weight, so the label names both rather than presenting the programme as a data-science degree.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The closest match applies the mathematics core to the modelling of natural and physical systems and to algorithms and optimisation. This alternative instead follows the evidenced probability-and-statistics and data-science study paths, organising the programme around learning from data. It therefore removes seven courses of the closest match — Ecosystems Uncovered, Earth System Science Tools, Robotics, Advanced Algorithms, Optimization Methods in AI, Decision-making in AI and Introduction to Western Philosophy — and adds seven that the data concept requires: Introduction to Data Science, Database Management Systems, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Econometrics, Reinforcement Learning, Earth Observation and AI Ethics. Epidemiology and image processing change role from modelling applications to data applications. The two programmes share seventeen courses and each contains 52.5 EC the other lacks.

alternatives.concept: A mathematics programme organised around VU's Optimisation and Economics study path: the shared mathematical foundation is carried into linear and non-linear optimisation, algorithmic optimisation, sequential decision-making under uncertainty and econometric estimation, and applied to formal economic theory of individual, strategic and market behaviour, public policy, the macroeconomy and corporate finance.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The closest match applies the mathematics core to the modelling of natural and physical systems; this alternative follows the evidenced Optimisation and Economics study path and applies the same foundation to economic behaviour and policy. It removes seven courses of the closest match — Ecosystems Uncovered, Epidemiology & Public Health, Sustainability Essentials I, Earth System Science Tools, Robotics, Image Processing & Computer Vision and Machine Learning — and adds Introduction to Economics, Microeconomics & Behavior, Public Economics, International Macroeconomics, Econometrics, Accounting & Corporate Finance and Reinforcement Learning, sharing seventeen courses with it. Against the statistics and data-science alternative it shares fifteen courses: the data-management, neural-network, satellite, image and data-ethics courses are replaced by economic theory and by optimisation and algorithm courses. In each pair every programme contains at least 52.5 EC the other lacks.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Mathematics bachelor. The 2026-2027 TER defines no formal specialisations, but the year-2 and year-3 constrained choices must be instantiated, and the official 2026-2027 study guide organises them into seven named, non-binding study paths that each satisfy the programme rules; one path is therefore used as a coherent valid pathway. The four interdisciplinary paths (Biomedical Mathematics, Computer Science, Data Science, Optimisation and Economics) add knowledge of another discipline - the TER learning outcome on another discipline applies only to students who follow them - and are more specialised than the three mathematics paths. Algebra and Geometry, Analysis and Dynamical Systems, and Probability and Statistics are equally general: the TER learning outcomes name algebra, geometry, analysis, dynamical systems, probability and statistics together as the main disciplines of mathematics, and none of the three is presented as the default. No path is clearly more representative, so the neutral tie-break selects Algebra and Geometry, the first path in the official order. The choice was fixed before UCR course selection and does not depend on UCR fit; it is in fact the path least represented in UCR's catalogue.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Introduction to Programming and Logic & Discrete Mathematics open the programme in semester 1, followed by Mathematical Methods in semester 2, which is the formal prerequisite of every later DISMATH course and of Robotics. Linear Algebra and Probability & Statistics in semester 3 precede Computational & Numerical Methods, Linear Systems, Advanced Algorithms and Robotics in semester 4, so numerical, transform and configuration-space methods follow matrix methods. Algorithms & Data Structures in semester 3 precedes Advanced Algorithms in semester 4. Research Methods & Statistics (semester 2) precedes the multivariate Statistics & Experimental Methods (semester 3), and both precede Machine Learning (semester 5) together with Linear Algebra and Probability & Statistics. Advanced Calculus is offered only in the second semester of a year and requires Mathematical Methods; semester 4 is filled by four courses offered only then, so semester 6 is its earliest feasible placement. Sustainability Essentials I in semester 1 is the formal prerequisite of Earth System Science Tools in semester 6; Ecosystems Uncovered is taken early as an introductory ecology course whose modelling component needs no formal mathematics prerequisite. Optimization Methods in AI and Image Processing & Computer Vision are placed in semester 6, after linear algebra, numerical methods and Linear Systems. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite falls in an earlier semester.

Advanced Calculus is offered only in the second semester of a year and semester 4 is filled by courses offered only then, so it is taken in semester 6. progressionAssessment.rationale: Introduction to Programming, Logic & Discrete Mathematics and Introduction to Economics open the programme; Introduction to Economics precedes every later economics course that builds on it. Mathematical Methods and Research Methods & Statistics in semester 2 are the formal prerequisites of the DISMATH courses and of all BENECON 200- and 300-level courses respectively. Optimization Methods in AI is placed in semester 2: it requires only Introduction to Programming, and it introduces search, constraint satisfaction and linear programming before the later optimisation courses; its projects are revisited after Linear Algebra (semester 3) in Advanced Algorithms (semester 4), Decision-making in AI (semester 5) and Reinforcement Learning (semester 6). Algorithms & Data Structures in semester 3 precedes Advanced Algorithms in semester 4. Public Economics (semester 4) and Microeconomics & Behavior (semester 6) follow Introduction to Economics; Econometrics in semester 6 follows Probability & Statistics and Statistics & Experimental Methods. Advanced Calculus is offered only in the second semester of a year and semester 4 is filled by courses offered only then, so it is taken in semester 6. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite falls in an earlier semester.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the fourteen generator-eligible rows that describe the programme's shared core: understanding why mathematical theories are true, mathematical proof and rigorous argument, pure and applied mathematics, mathematical modelling and using mathematics to solve real-world problems, together with Algebra and Geometry (the study path instantiated as the comparator route) and Analysis and Dynamical Systems (whose analysis, dynamical-systems and Fourier content is compulsory for every student). UCR can implement the modelling, calculus, linear-algebra and dynamical-systems parts of this core but not proof-based analysis, abstract algebra, geometry or topology; these remain visible gaps rather than being replaced. The remaining ten generator-eligible rows form five specific candidate directions, each assessed separately. Probability and statistics with data science (clustered because VU's two paths share their statistics core and the data-science path builds statistical inference into learning from data) is evidenced by two study paths and implemented by UCR's statistics, econometrics, databases, machine-learning and neural-network courses; it shares seventeen courses with the closest match and is included second. Optimisation and economics is evidenced by its study path and implemented by UCR's optimisation, decision-making and algorithm courses together with microeconomic, public-economic, macroeconomic and econometric courses; it shares seventeen courses with the closest match and fifteen with the data-science alternative and is included third. These two were considered before the others because UCR offers dedicated course sequences whose content directly implements their paths' courses (machine learning, databases and mathematical statistics; linear programming, decisions under uncertainty and formal microeconomic theory). Computer science through mathematics was considered next: its mathematical core (logic and discrete mathematics, algorithms, advanced algorithms, programming) is already in the closest match, so a distinct version would rest on systems courses such as Networks & Operating Systems and Software Development; biomedical mathematics would rest on molecular life-science courses because UCR has no mathematical-biology course. Both are recorded as maximum-reached because three alternatives had already been included. Mathematics education and teaching is not feasible: the path leads to a Dutch secondary-school teaching qualification through an Education minor, and UCR offers no pedagogy, didactics or teacher-education courses. Production stops at the maximum of three alternatives.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both are the programme's opening single-variable calculus course on differentiation and integration. VU's course develops the theory behind these techniques; Mathematical Methods is technique-oriented and also covers complex numbers and differential equations.
Both extend calculus to functions of several variables. Advanced Calculus also treats differential equations and complex-valued functions.
Both are the dedicated discrete-mathematics course. UCR's course combines discrete structures with logic and applications to algorithm construction.

Basic Concepts in Mathematics is the first-year introduction to the language and argumentation of university mathematics. Logic & Discrete Mathematics treats logic but is already matched to Discrete Mathematics, and no UCR course is a dedicated introduction to writing proofs, so no counterpart is claimed.

Mathematical Analysis develops the rigorous theory behind differentiation and integration. UCR's calculus courses teach techniques and applications rather than proof-based analysis, so no counterpart is claimed.

Complex Analysis studies functions of a complex variable. Advanced Calculus touches complex-valued functions but is a calculus course already matched to Multivariable Calculus; UCR has no complex-analysis course.
UCR has no course on partial differential equations; its calculus and numerical courses treat ordinary differential equations only.
Both are the dedicated linear-algebra course: systems of linear equations, vector spaces, linear transformations and eigenvalues.
Group Theory is the first abstract-algebra course. UCR has no abstract-algebra course; Advanced Algorithms treats algebraic algorithms computationally and is not claimed as a counterpart.
Rings and Fields continues abstract algebra. UCR has no counterpart.
Galois Theory is an advanced abstract-algebra course. UCR has no counterpart.

Elements of Geometry is a geometry course taken as a practical exercise. UCR has no geometry course; Robotics uses geometric reasoning about configuration spaces for motion planning but is not a geometry course, so no counterpart is claimed.
Topology studies topological spaces and continuity abstractly. UCR has no counterpart.
Differential Topology is an advanced course on smooth manifolds. UCR has no counterpart.
Both treat Fourier series and the Fourier transform. Linear Systems approaches them through signals and linear time-invariant systems and adds the Laplace and Z-transforms.

Dynamical Systems is the core course on the mathematical theory of systems evolving in time. Linear Systems treats only linear time-invariant systems and is already matched to Fourier Analysis, and no other UCR course develops dynamical-systems theory, so no counterpart is claimed.

Mathematical Modelling of Dynamical Systems translates real systems, such as predator-prey populations, into dynamical models. Ecosystems Uncovered spends two weeks on ecological modelling and Earth System Science Tools teaches Earth-system modelling, but both are science courses in which modelling is one component rather than the mathematical subject itself, so neither is claimed as a counterpart.
Both are the mathematical-probability course: probability theory and discrete and continuous distributions. UCR's course also covers sampling, estimation and simulation.

Both teach statistical inference, including estimation and hypothesis testing. VU's Mathematical Statistics develops it mathematically; Research Methods & Statistics is an applied course paired with research design, so the row shares the subject and function but not the mathematical depth.

Mathematical Modelling of Stochastic Systems models random processes evolving in time. Decision-making in AI concerns planning under uncertainty rather than stochastic-process modelling, and Linear Algebra treats Markov chains only as an application, so no counterpart is claimed.
Both teach programming in Python from scratch. UCR's course is a full course that also covers object-oriented programming and elements of discrete mathematics; VU's is a 3-EC introduction.
Both are the dedicated numerical-methods course: numerical root finding, interpolation, differentiation, integration and differential equations, with attention to accuracy.

Introduction to Mathematical Modelling, LaTeX and Mathematica teaches mathematical software and typesetting for modelling work. UCR mathematics courses use computer algebra software within their content, but no UCR course is dedicated to mathematical software and typesetting.

Both address ethics as part of the programme. Philosophy and Ethics is a 3-EC course for science students; UCR's Ethics is a full course in moral theory and practical ethics and shares its ethical component, not any philosophy-of-science content.
History of Science is a 3-EC course on the historical development of science. No UCR course in these alternatives treats the history of science, so no counterpart is claimed.

The 30-EC third-year elective period is open profiling space (mathematics electives, a minor, the Education minor or study abroad) with no fixed content. It is preserved as open space and not matched to any UCR course.
The Bachelor Project Mathematics is an individual 12-EC research project and thesis. No scheduled UCR course is a thesis; UCR's optional independent research is shown in this row.

notes.text: The VU programme includes a more extensive sequence in pure mathematics: proof-based analysis, abstract algebra (Group Theory, Rings and Fields, Galois Theory), geometry and topology (Elements of Geometry, Topology, Differential Topology), complex analysis, dynamical systems, partial differential equations and the modelling of stochastic systems, together with a 12-EC bachelor project. At UCR, students can study calculus, advanced calculus, linear algebra, logic and discrete mathematics, probability and statistics, numerical methods and linear systems, and apply them in modelling, data science or optimisation, but UCR does not offer the same depth or sequence in mathematics.
